Definition: apparently a primary verb (perhaps akin to G1502 through the idea of faintness as a copy); to resemble:--be like.
BiblicalUsage: This word means to yield or give place, to step aside, and Paul uses it once. He says that to the false brethren who came to spy out their liberty, he gave place by subjection not even for an hour, so that the truth of the gospel might continue with the Galatians. One refusal to yield kept the gospel free.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe some ground must never be yielded, because the truth of the gospel is worth more than an hour of peace.
